correctness.rationale: Separate unrestricted-depth pebble-game arguments establish both directions. At width two, every vertex has an adjacent and a distinct nonadjacent alternative. For width k>=3, Duplicator injectively matches occupied components, sides, and vertices, using truncation at k to ensure any free component/side element exists after one pebble is lifted. For necessity, k pebbles on k or fewer distinct source components force a collision of replies when the other graph has fewer, which a spare or recycled third pebble exposes by the adjacency of a neighbor to one but not the other. The analogous h-pebble argument separates two side-threshold profiles, with h>=3. The side-threshold counts for h=3,...,k recover the unordered truncated pair; no h=2 distinction is possible because both sides have size>=2. Class counts, canonical minimum representatives, and sharp relative defining widths then follow. The finite colour-refinement checker has 45, 136, 55 model pairs at widths 2, 3, 4 with zero discrepancies; it is corroborative, not an infinite proof. A fresh script replay must be checked before delivery.

originality.rationale: The combined family has independent component count and unordered bipartition-side counts. Retrieved classic literature concerns pebble-game methods, while closest specialized records concern complete multipartite/connected bipartite graphs or unions of 4-cycles, each containing only a boundary slice of the claim. The exact three-parameter truncated equivalence and k^2(k-1)/2 theory census were not found in actual searches. This is a qualified originality judgment; an uninspected general composition theorem might imply the classification.
residual_risks: Historical priority is provisional; a stronger finite-variable Feferman–Vaught or disjoint-composition theorem may imply the exact result without naming these parameters.
Two highly relevant prior boundary cases are already covered: single bicliques and disjoint unions of four-cycles; novelty is claimed only for the combined interior and exact full spectrum.
The public multipartite published-finding corpus entry and Dawar–Holm text were not available for full-text comparison; only title/abstract-level evidence was used for those sources.
Earlier historical claim ledgers outside the accessible current and immediately prior periods were not retrieved, so unpublished overlap is incompletely surveyed.

value.rationale: The natural graph family nK_{a,b} has three independent multiplicities and no named components or sides; obtaining exact simultaneously sharp k-variable thresholds is a nontrivial interaction of symmetry and bounded-variable expressiveness. The collision-exposure lemma shows that detecting an unlabelled component/side mismatch does not cost an extra variable, unlike a naive formula that keeps an additional existential witness. All widths, exact cubic theory counts, canonical smallest representatives, largest minimum order, and strict hierarchy are supplied. This is a complete family classification, not a arbitrary finite slice or simple restatement of prior single-component/cycle cases.
